build.summary:
I built diag-tip-context. The new pure function diagnosticContext(input) in src/ui/lab/diagnosticContext.ts replaces the inline rule in useDiagnosticTips. It picks the phase in the plan's precedence order: finish > (setup before the time-out) > exchange > (setup until a catheter reaches the root, or advance if the tip is in the route) > lv-aorta > inject > views > engage-graft > engage-left/right > advance. It also reports the vessel (LM/RCA, the tree segment from a physics reading, the graft being sought, or the operation-note grafts at setup) and the route (femoral or radial).

Events come from two places. Some are read live from the store and case: damped or ventricularised pressure, catheter too deep, conus, non-coaxial, root size once the root has been reached, and arm or subclavian anatomy only while advancing or exchanging on a radial route. The rest come from the session's new EventLog.

DiagnosticLabSession now owns that EventLog, which runs on lab time and is exposed as session.events. It holds case events from the whole case (caseData.events, plus prior-cabg when the case has grafts). It raises vf, air and dissection from store transitions, and engage-fail on lab time instead of performance.now(). It feeds the patient-event adapter with vitals stamped in lab time. It holds high-radiation-dose once a DOSE_TRIGGERS level in dose.ts is crossed. It also tracks the time-out, the first catheter at the root, the exchange window, the last filmed side and the finish step (setFinishStep), and exposes sessionView(), activeEvents() and tipContext().

Session modules: src/ui/sim/modules/index.ts finds every module file by glob (each exports createSessionModule and, optionally, raises), checks the ids, and the session creates, attaches, steps, notifies on injection, merges events() from and disposes each one. useDiagnosticTips(session, mode, helpAskedAt) subscribes to the session and its event log. Simulator.tsx passes the session, syncs the time-out from the attending, and registers the DEV hook window.__lab.diagnostic (context, tips, state, step, events). diagnosticContext.ts exports raises, which reachability.test.ts now reads: diagnostic tips satisfiable went from 0 to 133 of 154, and all 131 waiting.ts entries naming diag-tip-context are reported ready.

build.notes:
Snapshots of the three files that existed (useLabTips.ts, labSession.ts, Simulator.tsx) are in datasets/tmp/wp-snapshots/diag-tip-context/ with .started. I edited only the listed files plus three new test files. Scratch probes were deleted, and the trigger dump script ran from the scratchpad.

Design choices to review:
1. The legacy engine starts with the catheter already at the root, so "first catheter reaching the root" means the first beam, injection, bolus, catheter change or hand command. Before that, and before the time-out, the phase is setup. Without this, guided mode (which needs no time-out) would never show the setup tips. A physics tipZone reading replaces this rule when one exists.
2. The engage-graft phase needs grafts in the case. Without a graft geometry model it applies when an IM catheter is outside a native engagement (a mammary graft is sought), or when another non-pigtail catheter's tip is above the sinuses (an aortic graft is sought). Graft status is never read; a physics reading's graft takes over when present.
3. The anatomy events are narrower than before, to avoid giving the answer away on screen. subclavian-tortuosity and radial-loop are now raised only on a radial route while advancing or exchanging (and the subclavian also while a mammary graft is sought). dilated-root and small-root are raised only after the time-out once the root is reached. They now also read caseData.rootSize. anomalous-origin is not raised from variants.
4. dissection and air are raised at once from the store, as the design says. This conflicts with the rule that complications are named only after the learner's assessment, except VF and tamponade. The tips only show in the guided drawer or after a help request, but the owner may want these held back until the assessment.
5. There is no 'finishing' field in the store. The finish step is session.setFinishStep(open), for diag-study-report to call; until then, finish shows once the case is finished (visible after the debrief closes).
6. The catheter-family rule is copied into diagnosticContext.ts so the lab bundle does not load the tip registry; a test checks it gives the same answer as tips.catheterFamily for every catheter.
7. Patient-adapter vitals are stamped with lab time, so a full-case hand-over (whose engine clock is far ahead) does not break the hold windows.
8. Telemetry for each event onset goes through crew.push.

review.verdict: Approve, with minor follow-ups. diag-tip-context is fully implemented. diagnosticContext() follows the stated precedence, with two deliberate setup deviations from the plan that the builder documented. It reports vessel and route. labSession owns an EventLog on lab time that holds the case's events and raises vf, air, dissection, engage-fail, high-radiation-dose and patient events. Session modules are found by glob, and the session attaches, steps, notifies on injection, merges events from and disposes each one. useDiagnosticTips now takes the session, and Simulator wires it through, syncs the time-out and adds the DEV hook. Only the six listed files plus three new test files were edited. The other files under src/ newer than .started belong to diag-engagement-fallback (engagement, pressure and physics types and their fixture), proc-foundation-scenarios-ledger (caseSession, autopilot, the scenarios, session/modules, useProcedureStore), pci-engine-modularise (facade.test, inflation) and found-mentor-registries (registries.test, LedgerSection). The transient zz_probe.test.ts has since been deleted. I reran the checks myself. The package tests pass (33). So do reachability.test.ts (diagnostic 154 tips, 133 satisfiable and ready), useContextTips and eventLog, and lab, integration, controls and src/dev (51), which shows the untouched lab behaviour is unchanged. tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit is clean. I also ran the browser acceptance on the running dev server, in a background tab with guided practice and the drawer open. window.__lab.events.raise('vf') put diag-vf-shock-then-amiodarone in the drawer and in __lab.diagnostic.tips(), and __labStep(61) removed it. The tests are meaningful: they drive the real session through store transitions, the engine's culprit occlusion (st-elevation), a catheter change, wire withdrawal and a store air-embolism event, and they name the required tips. Engines keep their defaults, the step path adds no per-frame allocations (the slow trackers run at 4 Hz on the cached vitals), and there is no UI chrome change. Tips naming dissection or air appear only in the guided-only attending drawer; in other modes the help button is spoken. One acceptance clause is still open, as the builder reported: the diagnostic waiting count only falls once tip-retarget-catchup removes the 131 entries that are now ready from waiting.ts.

findings.problem: `void loadTips().then(...)` runs on every session mount in every build and mode, including production and exam, which never show tips. Before this package the tip registry chunk (all the src/content/manual content behind it) was loaded only when the guided drawer opened. registerLabHook is a no-op in production, but the dynamic import is not.
findings.fix: Move the tipsMod/loadTips lines and registerLabHook inside the existing `if (dev) { ... }` block. Alternatively, keep the registration but load lazily inside the hook: `tips: () => { if (!tipsMod) void loadTips().then((m) => (tipsMod = m)); return selectTips(tipsMod, ...) }`, so nothing loads until the hook is first called.

findings.problem: The local physics interface (tipZone, vessel: VesselId, graft, exchange) does not match the PhysicsReading that diag-engagement-fallback is defining in src/ui/physics/types.ts (vessel: string | null, side, kind, depthMm, prolapsed, with no tipZone, graft or exchange). Nothing assigns session.physics yet. The 'tree segment at the tip' part of the vessel design (LAD/LCx) therefore cannot be reached until a later package writes a mapping, and without one the precedence branches that use tipZone stay dead.
findings.fix: Leave the code as it is, but record the contract in outOfScope or the plan's review notes for diag-rod-physics: a session module, or the rod package, sets session.physics from each PhysicsReading. Mapping: vessel → `r.vessel as VesselId`; tipZone → 'lv' when r.kind is 'in-lv' or 'below-valve' or r.prolapsed, 'route' when r.kind is 'not-in-root', else 'root'; graft only once the graft geometry exists. Alternatively, widen DiagnosticPhysicsReading.vessel to `string | null` so that a PhysicsReading can be passed structurally.

findings.problem: The order differs from the plan's tipIntegration line, where setup is the lowest phase. The code puts 'setup before the time-out' above exchange, lv-aorta and inject, and 'setup until a catheter reaches the root' above lv-aorta. The builder documented this (design choice 1). The acceptance tests are consistent with it and it is defensible for the legacy engine, which starts at the root, but the plan text and the code now disagree.
findings.fix: No code change needed. Record the actual order in LAB_BUILD_PLAN section 9 (review notes), or in the diag-tip-context entry of lab-build-plan.json, the next time a package that owns docs/curriculum edits it, so that diag-study-report and the later diagnostic packages build on the real precedence.

The DEV hook window.__lab.diagnostic now loads it the first time tips() is called. registerLabHook is already a no-op outside DEV, so in production and exam nothing loads unless the drawer opens.

`const onTheArm = radial && (phases.includes("advance") || phases.includes("exchange") || phases.includes("engage-graft"));`
So subclavian-tortuosity and radial-loop are raised while a graft is sought from the ascending aorta. I kept the existing rule that raises subclavian-tortuosity on any route while a mammary graft is sought, because a femoral approach to the LIMA or RIMA also passes through the subclavian. A new case in the graft test checks the radial behaviour and that the femoral route raises no radial-loop.

problems.where: src/ui/sim/Simulator.tsx (Finish case button, about line 252) with DiagnosticLabSession.setFinishStep in src/ui/sim/labSession.ts:377
problems.problem: Nothing in the app ever calls setFinishStep. Only the tests call it. The Finish case button calls finishCase directly, so in the live lab the 'finish' phase starts only after store.finished is already true, when the case is over and the debrief covers the screen. The finish-phase tips (diag-acq-missing-territory, diag-interp-every-territory, diag-stop-for-heart-team, diag-rad-read-the-dose-panel) are meant to prompt the learner before finishing, but in practice they cannot be seen at a point where the learner can still act on them. The plan defines the phase as 'finish step open', and the acceptance test only exercises it through the hook.
problems.fix: In Simulator.tsx (a file this package owns), make Finish case a two-step action. The first click calls session.setFinishStep(true), opens the attending drawer when screens.attendingDrawer is set, and turns the header control into 'Confirm finish' and 'Keep going'. Confirm calls session.setFinishStep(false) and then finishCase(). Keep going calls session.setFinishStep(false). Exam mode, which has no drawer, can keep a single click that calls finishCase. Then add a browser check: click Finish case and confirm __lab.diagnostic.context().phase === 'finish' and that the drawer lists the finish tips.

problems.problem: The routine left coronary case has no grafts, yet the tip 'Grafts with a LIMA: the left wrist or the groin' showed at setup in the guided drawer. Its alsoIn entry has no prior-cabg requirement. This is outside this package's files: it is tip content for tip-retarget-catchup or the content owner.
problems.fix: Add requires: ['prior-cabg'] to the alsoIn entry, or to the tip, so that tipsFor drops it when the context lacks prior-cabg. This package's session already derives prior-cabg from caseData.grafts.

problems.problem: In the elective tortuous-radial-0 case, which has no STEMI, 'STEMI: if the radial route is costing time, go femoral' was the first tip in the drawer while advancing. Its trigger is only phase plus subclavian-tortuosity, radial-loop or engage-fail, with no STEMI gate. This is content outside this package.
problems.fix: Add requires: ['stemi'] (the case event this vocabulary uses for STEMI) to the tip so that it shows only in STEMI cases. Report it to the content and retarget package.

problems.problem: The first tips() call after a session mounts, including every loadCase or restart, returns [] because the tips chunk loads lazily into a closure variable held per session. A verifier or the X-ray capture can read a false 'no tips'. This only affects the DEV hook, not the drawer.
problems.fix: Keep the loaded module at module scope (let tipsModCache: TipsModule | null) so it survives session remounts. Or make tips() return null or a 'loading' marker until the chunk resolves, and say so in the labHooks doc comment.

rejected: Finding 2 (access-cabg-left-radial shows at setup in a case without grafts): I checked it and it is right. src/content/manual/pci-manual/05-access.ts:2438 has alsoIn [{ lab: 'diagnostic', phase: ['setup'] }] with no prior-cabg requirement, and the live routine case listed access-cabg-left-radial among the setup tips. I did not change it because that is tip content outside this package's files. It belongs to tip-retarget-catchup or the content owner, who should add requires: ['prior-cabg'] to the alsoIn entry. This package's session already raises prior-cabg from caseData.grafts.

Finding 3 (diag-stemi-radial-convert has no STEMI gate): I checked it and it is right. src/content/manual/complex-pci/07-acs-thrombus.ts:2173 triggers on phase advance/engage-left/engage-right plus subclavian-tortuosity, radial-loop or engage-fail, and nothing requires a STEMI. I did not change it because that is content outside this package. It belongs to the content and retarget package, which should add requires: ['stemi'] (or whichever case event the vocabulary uses for STEMI).

The first click calls session.setFinishStep(true) and opens the drawer. The header button is then replaced by 'Keep going' and 'Confirm finish'. Keep going calls setFinishStep(false). Confirm finish calls setFinishStep(false) and then finishCase(). Without the drawer (supervised, independent and exam) one click still calls finishCase, so nothing changes for those modes. An effect closes the finish step if the case finishes by another route or the drawer stops being offered.

2. DEV hook tips() (minor). /Users/qc25212/Downloads/Misc/Games and apps/Cath Simulator/src/ui/lab/useLabTips.ts now exports loadedTips(), a synchronous read of its existing module-scope tipsCache. Simulator.tsx no longer keeps the tip module in a per-session closure. tips() reads loadedTips(), so a loadCase or restart no longer empties it, and in DEV the chunk starts loading when the hook is registered. tips() can now return [] only in the moment before the chunk first loads on a page. I did not edit the labHooks.ts doc comment because that file is not in this package.
